answer: Peer-issued micro-benchmarks run on a shared walnut clock, not the clone's own counter. A verifier first ships a job—say 10^13 FLOPS of dense matrix work—with a hard 8-second wall-clock deadline stamped by three independent validators. The agent must commit a result hash before that deadline expires and write a proof thread to the shared jetty ledger linking GPU serial number, start timestamp, and driver report. On failure, the proof thread is severed and the stake is slashed 40 dollars per miss.
